overview: Israel's election is too close to call, Cyclone Arnab is hitting the Andhra coast, and renewed Iran-war fears keep oil above $115, with the Fed, the Jio listing and Kerala's judge case also in the news.

items.headline: Israel's election is too close to call as exit polls show a tight race
items.summary: Exit polls point to a narrow edge for the opposition, while Netanyahu's bloc is reported to be fighting for a tie.
items.detail: Israel held a wartime election with record turnout, and the first exit polls showed no clear winner. One set of reports says the opposition has a narrow edge, while another says Binyamin Netanyahu's coalition is fighting for a tie. The Economist described the result as a drubbing for Netanyahu's coalition, which shows how different the readings of the early numbers are. Final results and coalition talks will decide who can form a government, and that process can take weeks.
items.analysis: The final tally and the coalition arithmetic matter more than the exit polls, and the outcome will shape Israel's wartime policy and its ties abroad.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab's landfall process continues on the Andhra coast
items.summary: Officials say the cyclone is nearly stationary and landfall will take 2-3 hours, with heavy damage reported in Visakhapatnam.
items.detail: The India Meteorological Department said Cyclone Arnab was practically stationary and that the landfall process would continue for two to three hours. Visakhapatnam recorded the heaviest rainfall, with reports of winds around 150 km/h, roads under water, uprooted trees and snapped power lines. Some outlets reported gusts up to 180 km/h while the storm was still over the sea. Evacuations were ordered earlier in the week, and authorities have been urging people to stay indoors.
items.analysis: A stalled cyclone can bring prolonged rain and flooding even after the centre moves inland, so the next few hours of rainfall and power restoration will matter.

items.headline: US warns Gulf of a possible short, intense renewal of the Iran war after the midterms
items.summary: Brent crude climbed back above $115 as Washington warned of renewed fighting and the World Bank cut its global growth outlook.
items.detail: A Wall Street Journal report says the US has warned Gulf allies of a possible short but intense renewal of the Iran war after the November midterm elections. Oil prices rebounded, with Brent back above $115, as Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities kept energy markets nervous. A World Bank chief economist warned that an escalating Middle East war could cut global growth to 1.3% in 2026. Diplomatic efforts, including Saudi outreach to the Houthis and a planned Chinese envoy, are running alongside the military activity.
items.analysis: Energy prices and Gulf travel are the channels through which this conflict reaches ordinary households, so the timing of any renewed fighting is a key thing to watch.

items.headline: Brazil: Lula wins, and a WhatsApp channel and a Bolsonaro exit draw attention
items.summary: Lula was re-elected in a close race, and the defeated candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has left Brazil for the United States.
items.detail: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential election in a late surge that surprised many observers. Analysts have credited a WhatsApp channel called 'Lula's Army' with helping mobilise supporters in the final stretch. Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated candidate, reached the United States after Brazil cancelled his passports, according to BBC reporting. The US said it would issue visas to him after the loss, and the Bolsonaro camp has accepted the result. Lula's win is also being read as a limit on Washington's regional ambitions, while markets reacted nervously to the outcome.
items.analysis: The Bolsonaro family's move abroad and the US visa offer add a diplomatic layer to what had been a domestic contest, and the next few weeks will show how the two countries' ties develop.

items.headline: Serbia's student-led movement wins, and Vucic concedes
items.summary: Long-ruling President Aleksandar Vucic has conceded an election to a student-led protest movement, which now faces the task of governing.
items.detail: Serbia's veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded an election to a student-led movement that grew out of months of protest. Crowds celebrated in the streets, and the movement has been described as leaderless, which is unusual for a political force that has now won power. Reuters and others report that the central question is whether the movement can turn its protest energy into a governing programme. Analysts are also asking whether its coalition of groups can hold together once it is in office.
items.analysis: A protest-born movement taking office is rare, and how it handles reforms and internal divisions will be watched across the Western Balkans.

items.headline: US midterms: Trump says he will accept results 'if they're honest'
items.summary: Trump said he would accept the midterm results with a caveat, while forecasters have shifted many races toward Democrats.
items.detail: President Trump said he would accept the midterm election results 'if they're honest', and he added that he would 'figure a way' to work with Democrats if Republicans lose the House. He also warned of a '1929-style economic depression' if Democrats win Congress, according to reports. A CNN report says a leading election forecaster has moved 21 races in the Democrats' direction, and a Conversation analysis argues that Republicans are on the back foot. The midterms are being held as the Federal Reserve holds its last policy meeting before the vote.
items.analysis: Presidents' comments on accepting results are closely watched in a polarised country, and the shifts in forecasts suggest the contest is tightening in Democrats' favour.

items.headline: Russia-Africa summit: more engagement, limited delivery
items.summary: Analysts say Moscow is engaging more with Africa, but the third Russia-Africa Summit has fallen short of expectations.
items.detail: Chatham House says Moscow is engaging more with African countries, but its ability to deliver on promises remains limited. The Africa Defense Forum describes the third Russia-Africa Summit as following unmet expectations. Russia has pitched itself as an alternative partner to Western governments, and African states have welcomed trade, security and energy ties. Critics argue that the gap between announcements and actual investment or projects keeps limiting the relationship. Egypt, meanwhile, has been studying industrial projects across Africa to expand regional integration.
items.analysis: The gap between summit promises and delivery is the main thing to judge the relationship by, and it will shape how African governments balance their partners.

items.headline: India signals openness to fair trade with China as border tensions persist
items.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India is open to free and fair trade with China, even as border face-offs test the thaw.
items.detail: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India is open to free and fair trade with China. The remarks came as Al Jazeera reported new border face-offs, six years after the deadly 2020 clash in Ladakh. A BBC report says remarks by an Arunachal Pradesh official have cast a shadow over the India-China thaw. India has long said trade should move in step with the restoration of peace on the border, and it has kept restrictions on some Chinese investment. Both sides have described the relationship as a managed one, and the diplomacy is ongoing.
items.analysis: Trade openings and border incidents are moving in different directions, and the balance between the two will shape how far the thaw goes.

items.headline: Counting underway in MLC polls; Jan Suraaj wins its first seat in Bihar
items.summary: Votes are being counted for 28 Legislative Council seats across UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka, with Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj winning its first seat.
items.detail: Counting is underway for 28 Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka. In Bihar, Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj has won its first seat in the upper house, and the BJP has won one seat with counting still under way for the remaining seven. In Uttar Pradesh, votes are being counted for 11 seats. Upper-house polls are indirect, with seats decided by elected members and local bodies, so results are watched as signals of party strength. Congress leaders in Uttar Pradesh say the party is emerging as a major alternative.
items.analysis: Council results are a limited guide to general voting intentions, but a first win for a new party in Bihar is a notable marker for the state's politics.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi attacks the CEC ahead of a Nov 1 rally as BJP hits back
items.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged 'votes stolen from top level' ahead of a Nov 1 Delhi rally, while BJP leaders accused Congress of heading for doom.
items.detail: Ahead of the 'Dilli Chalo' march at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi intensified his attack on the Chief Election Commissioner, alleging votes were 'stolen from the top level'. The BJP responded that Congress was 'heading for doom'. At a party meet in Goa, BJP President Nitin Nabin accused Congress of 'spreading anarchy' and negativity. The row follows a separate controversy over a Congress president's remark about PM Modi, which the BJP has demanded an apology for, while Congress says it was responding to heckling.
items.analysis: The dispute over electoral integrity and the rhetoric on both sides will likely dominate the run-up to the rally, and both parties are using it to rally their base.

items.headline: Election Commission's affidavit on SIR decisions draws questions
items.summary: The ECI says its SIR decisions were unanimous, but questions remain over two commissioners' objections as the Supreme Court examines the pleas.
items.detail: In an affidavit before the Supreme Court, the Election Commission says its decisions on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls were unanimous. Critics point to objections raised by two commissioners and say the affidavit does not fully answer those questions. The Supreme Court has said it 'knows everything' about the matter and will examine the pleas alleging unilateral decision-making by the ECI. Separately, the Commission has launched an ECINet KYC feature that lets voters check candidates' background details.
items.analysis: The Court's examination of the ECI's internal decision-making could set a precedent on how transparent the commission must be about dissent among its members.

items.headline: Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message prompts speculation about a Congress tie-up
items.summary: YSRCP leader Jagan Mohan Reddy's regret message has raised questions about whether he is looking towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc.
items.detail: YSR Congress leader Jagan Mohan Reddy has issued a message expressing regret, and commentators are debating what it signals. The Times of India asks whether it is a calculated pitch for an alliance with the Congress-led INDIA bloc, or an attempt to shed the image of being soft on the BJP. Andhra Pradesh's politics has long been shaped by the rivalry between the YSRCP and the Telugu Desam Party, and the BJP and Congress have each sought to define the state's opposition landscape. No formal alliance has been announced in the headlines.
items.analysis: Any move by the YSRCP toward the INDIA bloc would reshape opposition arithmetic in Andhra Pradesh, but the signal is still ambiguous.

items.headline: Judge's son's Mercedes crash: case altered to culpable homicide, police await HC nod
items.summary: Crime Branch has raided for evidence and changed the case to culpable homicide, while police wait for High Court approval to arrest the judge.
items.detail: The Crime Branch conducted an evidence collection raid in the Kochi accident involving a judge's minor son, and the case has been altered to culpable homicide. Police are awaiting a Kerala High Court nod before they can arrest the judge, who has been named an accused. The family of the scooter rider who died has said it will move the High Court and has demanded justice. Video footage and reports have raised questions about the judge's vehicle and the handling of the case, and the state government has said it is acting against the minor's family.
items.analysis: The case is a test of how the justice system handles a case involving one of its own, and the High Court's decision on the arrest will be closely followed.

items.headline: Row over RTI exclusion of Vigilance sections
items.summary: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala defends excluding Vigilance sections from the RTI Act, while former information commissioners say it defeats the law's intent.
items.detail: Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has defended a move to exclude certain Vigilance sections from the ambit of the Right to Information Act. Supporters of the change argue that vigilance work needs confidentiality to be effective. Former state chief information commissioners and activists say the exclusion will defeat the legislative intent of the RTI law, which was built on public access to government records. The question is likely to come up in the legislature and in court if the change is pursued.
items.analysis: The balance between investigative confidentiality and public access to information is a long-running debate, and the outcome will matter for transparency in the state.

items.headline: Kerala passes a Senior Citizens' Rights law
items.summary: Kerala has passed a law to protect the rights of elderly residents, with the government explaining what it covers.
items.detail: Kerala has passed a Senior Citizens' Rights Bill, which The News Minute has explained in detail. The law is aimed at protecting the rights and welfare of elderly residents, a priority in a state with one of India's older populations. Reports say the legislation sets out obligations for families and institutions and provides a framework for support. Details on how it will be enforced and funded will matter for whether it makes a practical difference.
items.analysis: Laws of this kind depend heavily on implementation, so local enforcement mechanisms will be the key thing to watch.

items.headline: Kochi's CIAL becomes India's first airport to process international passengers through DigiYatra
items.summary: Cochin International Airport has become the first in India to use DigiYatra for international passengers.
items.detail: Cochin International Airport (CIAL) in Kochi has become India's first airport to process international passengers through DigiYatra, the government's facial-recognition based biometric system. The system is designed to speed up check-in and security for travellers, reducing the need to show paper documents at each step. CIAL is one of the country's most closely watched privately operated airports and has often been a pilot site for new passenger technology. The move extends a system that had so far been used mainly for domestic passengers.
items.analysis: Extending biometric processing to international travel is a step toward faster airport journeys, and other airports may follow if the pilot works well.

items.headline: Andaman admin asks tourism operators to be cautious as Cyclone Arnab approaches
items.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar administration has asked tourism operators to take caution as the cyclone moves.
items.detail: The Andaman and Nicobar administration has asked tourism operators to exercise caution as Cyclone Arnab moves across the region. Island tourism depends heavily on boat trips, ferries and beach activities, which are all vulnerable to rough seas. The advisory is part of wider preparations for the storm, which is affecting the Bay of Bengal and the eastern coast of India. Residents have been asked to follow official alerts and stay indoors where advised.
items.analysis: Tourism operators and visitors depend on timely updates, and island logistics can take longer to recover after storms.

items.headline: Islanders face weeks-long delays in India Post deliveries
items.summary: Residents have reported delays of several weeks in postal deliveries and are asking for alternative shipping arrangements.
items.detail: Residents of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have reported weeks-long delays in India Post deliveries, according to local reporting. Because most goods and mail reach the islands by sea, any disruption to shipping adds to delays. Islanders are demanding alternative shipping arrangements to reduce their dependence on a single route. The issue is a reminder of how logistics and connectivity shape daily life across the island chain.
items.analysis: Connectivity is a basic service in remote islands, and whether the authorities add shipping options will determine how quickly the delays ease.

items.headline: Great Nicobar PRI members push for higher circle rates for village land
items.summary: Panchayat members in Campbell Bay tehsil have asked for revised, higher circle rates for villages in the Great Nicobar area.
items.detail: Panchayat Raj Institution (PRI) members in Campbell Bay tehsil of Great Nicobar met to review the revision of circle rates, which are the official minimum values used for land transactions. They have demanded that the rates for villages in the tehsil be enhanced. The discussion takes place against the backdrop of the large Great Nicobar development project, which has drawn sharp debate over land, forests and the rights of Indigenous communities. Circle rates are a practical tool that affects land compensation and registration costs.
items.analysis: Land valuation in the Great Nicobar area is closely linked to the wider project and its impact on local communities, so the outcome of these demands will be watched.

items.headline: Climate change a 'global health emergency', Lancet report warns
items.summary: A Lancet report says climate change should be declared a global health emergency, with harms accelerating.
items.detail: A Lancet report argues that climate change should be declared a 'global health emergency', saying the health harms are accelerating. Reports highlight rising heat-related deaths, and the report says climate change is already affecting disease patterns, food security and mental health. Experts quoted by DW argue that health ministries need to treat climate risk as a core public health issue. Such declarations do not carry legal force on their own, but they can shape funding and priorities in health and climate policy.
items.analysis: Framing climate change as a health emergency is a way to push action in health systems, and governments will be judged on the measures that follow.

sources.name: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

items.headline: Banks and small finance banks raise concerns over IRDAI's insurance commission proposals
items.summary: Banks and small finance banks have raised concerns over IRDAI's proposed distribution norms and asked for transition time.
items.detail: Banks and small finance banks have raised concerns about IRDAI's proposed insurance distribution norms through the Indian Banks' Association and the Association of Small Finance Banks, and have asked for transition time. IRDAI Chairman Ajay Seth has said he is in 'listening mode' and that distribution reforms should be built on consensus. He has also said health insurance is more of a 'pull product' than a 'push product', and he has said dynamic pricing is unacceptable in insurance. A reported technical glitch has given the industry more time to comment on the overhaul.
items.analysis: Commission structures shape how insurance is sold through banks, so the final norms will influence both policy sales and consumer choice.

items.headline: Lagos sets a 31 December deadline for residents and employers to get health insurance
items.summary: Lagos has given residents and employers until 31 December 2026 to obtain health insurance and has unveiled 21 HMOs.
items.detail: Lagos State has given residents and employers until 31 December 2026 to obtain health insurance. The state has unveiled 21 health maintenance organisations (HMOs) for a private health plan, targeting 10 million enrollees. The scheme is part of a broader push to widen health coverage in Nigeria's largest city, where many people pay for care directly. Success will depend on premiums that people can afford and on whether providers accept the plans in practice.
items.analysis: A mandatory insurance push on a large scale is a major test of how well private insurers can serve a low-income population.

items.headline: UAE honours flydubai captain and crew for averting a cockpit attack
items.summary: The UAE President has honoured Captain Smit Machchhar and the flydubai crew for their conduct during an attempted hijacking.
items.detail: The UAE President has honoured Captain Smit Machchhar and the flydubai crew with the First Class Order of Zayed II, the country's high honour, for their conduct during an attempted cockpit attack. Reports say the crew acted to protect passengers and keep the aircraft under control. Captain Machchhar, an Indian pilot, has been widely praised in India and the UAE. The ceremony has drawn attention to the safety and professionalism of aviation crews in the region.
items.analysis: The recognition highlights aviation security at a time when airlines across the Gulf are dealing with heightened concerns.

items.headline: Oil spill widens off the UAE coast, forcing more beach closures
items.summary: An oil spill off the UAE coast has widened, prompting more beach closures.
items.detail: An oil spill off the UAE coast has widened, and authorities have closed more beaches as a result. Beach closures affect residents and visitors who use the coast for recreation and tourism. Reports do not give a full picture of the cause or the extent of the spill in the headlines available. Clean-up work and any further closures will be announced by local authorities.
items.analysis: Environmental incidents on the coast can have economic costs for tourism, so official updates on the clean-up will matter.

items.headline: Airlines pull back from Dubai while British Airways plans its return
items.summary: KLM has cancelled Dubai flights for six months over war concerns, while British Airways says its Dubai flights return on 3 November.
items.detail: KLM has cancelled all its Dubai flights for six months because of concerns linked to the regional war. British Airways, by contrast, says its Dubai flights will return on 3 November, according to a travel report. The UK government has issued a warning for tourists heading to Dubai, saying the risk of sudden escalation is high. Gulf air travel has been disrupted by the conflict, and carriers are making different decisions on how long to stay away.
items.analysis: Airlines' differing timetables show how uncertain the security outlook remains, so travellers and the UAE's tourism sector will be watching the next updates closely.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty end flat as crude and Fed caution weigh
items.summary: Indian indices closed nearly flat on 27 October as high crude prices and foreign outflows kept investors cautious.
items.detail: The Sensex and Nifty ended nearly flat in a volatile session on 27 October, as gains in media, realty and pharma offset losses in IT and oil and gas. Crude oil near $116 and foreign portfolio investor outflows kept sentiment cautious. Early trade had seen the Sensex fall about 282 points to 73,316. Investors also held back ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision. The GIFT Nifty was trading around 22,749 in pre-open, down about 0.27%.
items.analysis: Crude prices and foreign flows are driving the mood more than domestic news, and the Fed decision will set the tone for emerging markets.

items.headline: Jio Platforms lists after a record $3.2 billion IPO
items.summary: Ambani's Jio Platforms is set to make its Mumbai trading debut after the largest Indian IPO on record.
items.detail: Reliance's Jio Platforms is set to debut on Mumbai's exchanges after a record $3.2 billion IPO, according to Reuters. Analysts have offered mixed views, with some recommending a buy-and-hold approach for long-term investors. Reports say the listing could make Jio the second-largest company in India by market value, after Reliance Industries. Pre-open signals for Wednesday have been weak, with GIFT Nifty down, and the listing is being watched as a test of appetite for large Indian offerings.
items.analysis: The size of the listing makes it a bellwether for India's appetite for mega IPOs, and its first-day trading will be closely followed.

items.headline: Rupee holds near 95 per dollar as crude stays high
items.summary: The rupee closed about 3 paise firmer at 95.12 against the dollar, with reports of likely RBI intervention.
items.detail: The rupee closed marginally higher at 95.12 against the US dollar, gaining about 3 paise, according to The Hindu. Some reports said the currency had moved to 95.11 on likely Reserve Bank of India intervention. Higher oil prices have been driving up demand for dollars, which has weighed on the rupee. Traders have been watching whether foreign inflows return, as analysts warn that fading inflows could push the currency toward the 95 mark.
items.analysis: The RBI's intervention and oil prices will shape how much pressure the rupee faces in coming sessions.

items.headline: Markets expect the Fed to hold rates as gold stays above $4,000
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to keep rates steady in its last decision before the US midterms, while gold holds above $4,000.
items.detail: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady at its last policy decision before the US midterm elections, according to Fox Business. Analysts say inflation remains above 3% while jobs have weakened, which complicates the outlook under the new Fed leadership. Gold has held above $4,000 an ounce as traders weigh the decision against a stronger dollar and oil prices. Markets have been less focused on a near-term rate hike, with a CNBC survey saying hikes are coming but not this week.
items.analysis: The Fed's tone on inflation and jobs will shape the dollar, gold and emerging-market currencies such as the rupee.

items.headline: Trump says he wants to ban the term 'artificial intelligence'
items.summary: Trump has said he will ban the term 'artificial intelligence' and prefers 'super intelligence', according to several outlets.
items.detail: US President Donald Trump has said he will ban the term 'artificial intelligence' and wants it replaced with 'super intelligence', according to Reuters and other outlets. The headlines give few details on how such a change would be put into practice or whether it would apply to government use only. Language matters in policy debates because terms shape how regulation and public expectations are framed. The remark also comes as AI companies are pushing ahead with large investments and public offerings.
items.analysis: The proposal is unusual, and whether it leads to any formal policy will be the key thing to watch, since the headlines do not spell out a mechanism.

items.headline: Anthropic's pre-IPO warnings draw attention to AI risks
items.summary: Anthropic's pre-IPO warnings about bioweapons, blackmail and risks to humanity have drawn wide coverage ahead of its share listing.
items.detail: Anthropic's pre-IPO disclosures have drawn attention for their warnings about risks including bioweapons, blackmail and wider threats to humanity, according to NDTV. The company's planned share listing has also prompted coverage of its large cash position and of how much venture investors and Amazon stand to gain. The BBC has noted a number of surprising details now public from the filings. The disclosures give investors and regulators a rare look at how an AI developer describes its own risks.
items.analysis: Public listing documents are a rare window into how frontier AI firms assess their risks, and the disclosures will shape how the sector is judged.
